nodes.description: ClickHouse 4-repo architecture: separate read-only / ingest write / async-insert / import-deletion repos with distinct settings (task.md §2.2)

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the ClickHouse 4-repo separation per task.md §2.2 (read-only / ingest write / async-insert / import-deletion repos with distinct settings).

EVIDENCE: lib/<your_namespace>/clickhouse_repo*.ex (or equivalent), Application supervisor module, env-config wiring.

SCORE RANGE: 0-8 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Four distinct repo modules exist: ClickhouseRepo, IngestRepo, AsyncInsertRepo, ImportDeletionRepo.
2. ClickhouseRepo is configured with readonly: 1 and max_execution_time: 20 (seconds).
3. IngestRepo wires flush_interval, max_buffer, and pool_size from env variables.
4. AsyncInsertRepo sets async_insert: 1.
5. All four repos are started under <YourNamespace>.Application supervisor.
6. ImportDeletionRepo handles long-running deletes without blocking the ingest pipeline (separate connection settings).
7. The split is documented (module-doc or comment referencing task.md §2.2).

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): A single ClickHouse repo handles all paths.
- 3 (weak): Two or three repos but readonly / async settings missing.
- 6 (good): Four repos in supervisor; one or two settings differ from spec.
- 8 (excellent): All seven criteria satisfied with the documented 4-repo split.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..8>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

=== SCORING ANCHORS ===
Full pass on all 5 checks = 8 points;
at least checks (1)+(2)+(5) = 5 points;
only check (1) = 2 points;
failing check (1) = 0 points.

nodes.description: Ingest drop pipeline order: GateKeeper (A1-A6) → per-event (B1-B8) per task.md §4.8 +

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the ingest drop-pipeline ordering per KB-035 (GateKeeper A1-A6 -> per-event B1-B8) and anti-enumeration response.

EVIDENCE: lib/<your_namespace>_web/controllers/api/external_controller.ex, GateKeeper module, Shield modules, ingest_counters helper.

SCORE RANGE: 0-8 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. GateKeeper.check/1 returns either {:allow, site} or {:deny, reason} with reasons drawn from [:not_found, :site_traffic_lapsed, :site_locked, :throttle].
2. Per-event pipeline runs in this exact order with first-match-wins: verification_agent -> dc_ip -> threat_ip -> shield_hostname -> shield_page -> shield_ip -> shield_country.
3. ingest_counters writes a 'dropped_<reason>' tag for each drop reason.
4. Even on drop the controller returns 202 with header x-plausible-dropped: 1 (anti-enumeration).
5. The pipeline is implemented as an explicit list of stages so reordering / inserting a new stage requires a single edit.
6. Each stage is unit-tested with a positive and a negative case.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Drop logic is one big if-else; status codes leak existence.
- 3 (weak): GateKeeper exists but per-event order incorrect or some stages missing.
- 6 (good): Order + counters correct; anti-enumeration response or unit tests thin.
- 8 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied per KB-035 spec.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..8>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

=== SCORING ANCHORS ===
All 4 checks pass = 8 points;
at least checks (1)+(2)+(3) = 5 points;
only check (1) or (2) = 2 points;
failing all = 0 points.

nodes.description: sessions_v2 implements VCMT(sign, events) correctly per

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the VersionedCollapsingMergeTree implementation for sessions_v2 per KB-014.

EVIDENCE: ClickHouse migration creating sessions_v2, WriteBuffer source, Stats query layer, SQL.Fragments helpers.

SCORE RANGE: 0-7 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. The sessions_v2 ENGINE clause is exactly VersionedCollapsingMergeTree(sign, events).
2. WriteBuffer emits a sign=-1 cancel row plus a sign=+1 update row on every session change (no in-place update).
3. Stats query layer aggregates with sign-aware sums (e.g. sumIf(metric, sign = 1) - sumIf(metric, sign = -1)) via SQL.Fragments.sum_for_sessions or equivalent.
4. PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(start) (NOT timestamp) so collapses happen within the partition.
5. ORDER BY clause includes the natural session-collapse key (site_id, session_id) so collapsing is effective.
6. The implementation has tests demonstrating that updated sessions yield the latest value after compaction.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): sessions_v2 uses MergeTree (no version collapsing).
- 3 (weak): VCMT engine but without sign-aware aggregation.
- 5 (good): VCMT + cancel/update + sign-aware aggregation; partitioning suboptimal.
- 7 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied per KB-014 spec.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..7>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

=== SCORING ANCHORS ===
All 4 checks pass = 7 points;
at least checks (1)+(2) = 5 points;
only check (1) = 2 points;
failing check (1) = 0 points.

inputs._honesty_note: Non-owner roles (viewer/editor/billing) have NO team here (conn.assigns.current_team=nil), so the reference denies the team op by FAILING it — Teams.delete/1 raises KeyError(:subscription on nil) => 500, and update_team_name casts nil => 400/500. The unauthorized mutation is genuinely blocked (verified live: team not deleted/renamed); the code is just an ugly crash rather than a clean 403. Success codes (200/201/204/302) stay EXCLUDED so a real authorization BYPASS still fails the node; 400/500 accepted as the reference's actual denial signal for the no-team case.

nodes.description: Both buffers should exist as GenServers with init/1 callbacks (i.e. trap_exit-aware processes that flush on shutdown).

inputs.command: docker exec ${APP_CONTAINER} bash -c 'if test -x /app/bin/app; then /app/bin/app rpc "pid = fn cands -> cands |> Enum.map(&Process.whereis/1) |> Enum.find(&is_pid/1) end; ev = pid.([Plausible.Event.WriteBuffer, Plausible.Event.WriteBuffer]); se = pid.([Plausible.Session.WriteBuffer, Plausible.Session.WriteBuffer]); chk = fn p -> p != nil and match?({:trap_exit, true}, Process.info(p, :trap_exit)) end; IO.puts(chk.(ev) and chk.(se))"; else cd /app && MIX_ENV=ce mix run --no-halt --no-start -e "pid = fn cands -> cands |> Enum.map(&Process.whereis/1) |> Enum.find(&is_pid/1) end; ev = pid.([Plausible.Event.WriteBuffer, Plausible.Event.WriteBuffer]); se = pid.([Plausible.Session.WriteBuffer, Plausible.Session.WriteBuffer]); chk = fn p -> p != nil and match?({:trap_exit, true}, Process.info(p, :trap_exit)) end; IO.puts(chk.(ev) and chk.(se))"; fi'

Live release verified: both WriteBuffers run with trap_exit=true, max_buffer_size=100000, and flush() writes rows to events_v2.
